article.name: Hestia
article.summary: Hestia is a local-first household assistant with two distinct memory paths: Markdown soft facts/preferences and structured SQLite entities/events. Its conversational memory supports direct writes and lexical recall; background extraction proposes facts for human approval. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

who_what.text: The official README presents Hestia as a local-first, self-hosted household assistant with one brain, a local LLM endpoint, and scoped tools. The repo is an integrated assistant application, not a standalone memory service.

The README distinguishes conversational soft facts/preferences from structured SQLite records such as pets, garden, wildlife, and chores. This review focuses on the soft-fact memory and its human-reviewed background proposal flow.

architecture.text: Soft-fact memory is one Markdown file per record under the configured memory directory. YAML frontmatter stores id, type, confidence, source, last_seen, links, and pinned; the body stores free text. INDEX.md is regenerated from the record files and is a derived listing.

A separate SQLite records store models entities, aliases, relations, and timestamped events. The README and records-store module distinguish this relational/event history from conversational memory; household state is queried from Home Assistant rather than stored as a soft fact.

The memory context builder searches the shared store using the current user text and injects relevant hits into the prompt with record ID, source, and last-seen date. The model-facing memory tool independently exposes write and recall operations.

The background note-taker reads a recent transcript after the foreground answer, asks a model for up to two durable household facts, and writes candidate Markdown into an inbox. The current design document labels its earlier auto-write/vector plan historical and points readers to the current harness behavior.

behavior.text: Direct write accepts a content string and one of seven types, creates a slug-derived unique ID, records source and date metadata, writes a Markdown file, and rebuilds INDEX.md. An ID collision gets a numeric suffix; the inspected write path does not compare meaning or replace an existing record.

Direct recall tokenizes the query and record ID/body/links, removes a fixed stop list, and scores term matches using corpus rarity and document-length normalization. Pins break ties only after a relevant match. Results default to five and are capped at twenty; context injection truncates each memory body to 1,200 characters.

No update or delete operation is exposed by the model-facing memory tool. The inspected write method always creates a new record. A person with filesystem access can edit or remove a live Markdown record; the source inspection found no soft-fact supersession history, tombstone, or dedicated delete API.

Background extraction is best-effort and bounded: it skips short user turns, caps proposals at two, normalizes model output, rejects system-talk and wishes/tasks, and deduplicates against live records and inbox items with keyword overlap. Novel proposals remain outside live recall until a person reviews them.

A person can keep, edit-and-keep, or discard an inbox proposal in the app; the CLI offers promote and discard. Promotion writes a new live memory with source `reviewed` and removes the proposal file; discard removes only the proposal. Edited text is bounded and rechecked by the note-taker's deterministic filters.

The note-taker failure path logs an error and returns without failing the already completed conversation. It can defer work to the model-job queue when the backend is deferred, and exposes environment controls for disabling extraction or selecting a local model/server.

metrics.evidence: Lexical recall and a prompt instruction to recall saved facts are present; answer accuracy and abstention were not scored.
No update operation was found in the model-facing memory path; human editing or a new write is possible, but correction sequences and stale-value rates were not measured.
A person can remove a Markdown file, but no model delete operation or post-delete probe was run; erasure from backups or other copies is unknown.
The soft-fact directory is shared household state without a per-user or tenant key in the inspected store; no cross-user or cross-household isolation workload was run.
Injected context includes a source label and last-seen date, but not a source passage or conversation reference; no generated answer was adjudicated for evidence support or citations.
No timings or write-to-recall probes were collected.
The source describes local Markdown storage and local-model extraction options; this review measured no tokens, cost, or storage boundary.

limits.text: The review inspected the official README, memory design and harness documentation, and selected current store, note-taker, review, API, tool, configuration, and prompt-assembly source at the verified head. Hestia, its tests, and benchmarks were not run.

The memory store has no tenant authorization key; the repository's security model instead says the brain has no built-in authentication and must remain behind a private network boundary. This review did not test deployed network controls or filesystem permissions.

The record `source` is a label/date rather than a retained source quote or conversation ID. The inspection does not establish that stored facts are true, that lexical recall handles paraphrases, or that file deletion removes copies from backups.

The historical MEMORY-DESIGN.md describes vector recall and git-versioned memory, while it labels itself a historical plan; current inspected store code is lexical, and the README/SECURITY documentation says private household memory data is gitignored. The deployed data configuration was not inspected.

benchmark.note: No Hestia runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed. All required metric domains remain unmeasured for this review; project metric definitions, fixture, and shared execution-status record are protocol/status documents, not Hestia measurements.
